summary: Helena NF 30-ft pole lookout dated 1941 (a 2003 item says 1930s), staffed in 1941, burned in the 2003 Snow-Talon Fire; a 2016 blog found debris on the summit.

facts.status_note: Burned in the 2003 Snow-Talon Fire. A 2016 blog found fire debris on the summit.

staffing.status: Staffed in the 1941 fire season (November 1941 item). A July 1948 item says a contracted plane would replace the lookout.

access.note: A 2016 blog describes a maintained trail to the summit. No source gives official visiting rules.

visit.trail_note: Reached from the Indian Meadows Trailhead via Copper Creek Road, per a 2016 blog

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1941; a 2003 item quoted on the Montana lookouts site says built in the 1930s. The story gives 1941 and reports the 2003 claim. A 1939 item shows the site was being proposed that year.

notes_for_editor: helenair.com (2003 fire articles) and mtstandard.com (residents' memories) returned HTTP 429 on two fetch attempts and are not cited; they may add detail on the 2003 fire and the build date. County conflict: firelookout.com says Lewis & Clark County; the NGS entry quoted on the Montana lookouts page says Granite; the story names no county. Height 30 ft from firelookout.com is recorded as height_m 9.1 (30 ft = 9.14 m). The 2016 blog is a personal account, used for the summit's state and the trail; it is not an official site record. The 2003 'built in the 1930s' claim is a newspaper recollection; the 1941 date is firelookout.com's. Edits 2026-10-10: the 1939 item says a need is shown for Silver King among points, not that a lookout was needed, so the story now says that; the 1941 item spells the fire lookout's name 'Jauroon' once and 'Jauron' once, and the story uses 'Jauron'; the 1958 ride was a three-day ride, and the 1948 claim about staffing rests on the item's comparison of aerial detection with men in lookout towers; the blog's 'Forest Service electronic site' and 'incinerated' wording and the item dates were added to the evidence.
